I have battled depression for over 20 years. I thought I had a handle on my illness, but this week has just brought back all of my fears and sorrow. My ex-wife and her new husband have taken my daughter to Disney in Florida. The divorce four years ago ruined me financially. I'll probably never be able to afford a trip like that for my daughter and I.

I have friends on the West Coast of the US. They always tell me to go out there. I don't like spending money on myself because I want to make sure I have it for my daughter. But, is that really the case or am I just afraid? I am always alone. I really only have my mother in my life. My friends, like I said, are in other states. I just hide myself in my home. What if I mess up? What if something goes wrong?

Tomorrow, Wed July 15, I had wanted to drive an hour and half to a state park and hike, but now I am terrified. I am talking myself out of going.

I am so tired of being afraid all the time.

(Sorry if this was a rambling post, or if it technically isn't depression.)
I am scared to face life. I am scared to be a failure.

I you have friends out of state that are inviting you to visit them, then totally do it, please. Support networks are so essential. Every time I'm in a really shitty spot, and I manage to reach out to someone, it so often just radically shifts my mood. Though I suppose if you're dealing with decades long depression, then it might not pull you out of it as much. But still, friends are invaluable. Visit them, spill your heart out, forget about your ex, and let them show you a good time!
They are true friends. They care more about me then my brothers.
Go seeeeee themmmm!!! What's keeping you from going out there? Is there any way you can overcome it?

Don't make the mistake my father made. He left me for eight years to try and "better" himself because he saw he thought he was failing his family. He comes back, only to leave again to try and find a job in another state.

My advice is this: be there for your child, even if you don't feel good enough. I'd rather see my dad than have is money.
